#!/usr/bin/env bash
# load_drop_retry.sh — bounded loopback-ws load-drop retry for sharded
# dart test legs (issue #2331).
#
# Family: under CI-leg load the dart test loader's loopback WebSocket
# (127.0.0.1:…/ws) to a freshly spawned test VM can die mid-handshake —
#   Failed to load "<file>": Connection closed before full header was
#   received, uri = http://127.0.0.1:…/ws
#   Failed to load "<file>": Connection reset by peer, uri=http://127.0.0.1:…/ws
# The victim file is arbitrary (whatever is loading when the socket dies),
# never an assertion failure (10/10 occurrences on the card). The shard reds
# even though every test that ran was green.
#
# This wrapper runs the shard's dart test command as given, and on failure
# that carries BOTH the `Failed to load "<path>"` marker AND a ws-drop
# signature, re-runs the failed inventory (the gh-1026
# rerun-only-failed-files discipline): the ws-dropped files PLUS every
# failed suite the failing attempt's reporter log records (the repo's
# scripts/gate_failed_targets.py). A co-occurring real failure — assertion
# failure or compile-error load failure — is therefore IN the rerun and
# keeps the shard red; an attempt whose only failures are ws drops heals.
# Without the ws-drop signature the wrapper never reruns at all: real
# failures stay loud, nothing is rerun blind, nothing is masked.
#
# Bounded retry (not one-shot; PR #2347 shipped the one-shot ancestor):
# every RED attempt whose OWN output carries the signature buys one more
# rerun of THAT attempt's failed inventory, up to
# $LOAD_DROP_RETRY_MAX_RERUNS (default 2 — three attempts total), after a
# drain backoff of $LOAD_DROP_RETRY_BACKOFF_S seconds (default 5, doubling
# per rerun). Detection reads only the failing attempt's own console
# segment — a healed file's old signature line can never re-arm the loop.
# The bound is hard: a drop-always runner reds after the last rerun with
# that attempt's exit code.
#
# Family 2 (gh-2381, run 45200064457 PTY shard 2/3): the same load class can
# kill the VM-service connection DURING a post-suite coverage gather; the
# test_core engine's run loop dies with the suite queue still pending —
# tests left IN FLIGHT (their tearDowns never run → live pty2 children)
# and whole suites never loaded — while the file-reporter records only the
# finished subset (allSuites count 26, 16 suite events, testStart 101 vs
# testDone 98). The abandoned pty2 `_waitForExitCode` isolates then block
# the VM's exit handshake forever (`Attempt:N waiting for isolate
# _waitForExitCode to check in`) and the shard burns its WHOLE budget
# before the timeout kill lands `cancelled`. The wrapper heals this shape
# inside the SAME bounded budget: the gh-2381 projections
# (gate_failed_targets.py --unfinished/--loaded) treat unfinished tests and
# never-loaded invocation targets as transient losses (trusted ONLY when
# the attempt's reporter log exists — a missing log never widens the
# inventory), and an exit-handshake WATCHDOG bounds the burn: sustained
# `Attempt:N waiting for isolate` spam on THIS attempt's fresh console
# output means the results are already recorded (the reporter flushes per
# event; coverage is per-suite incremental), so the wedged runner's
# process group is SIGKILLed and the loop's evidence-driven decision
# proceeds. The spam budget is $LOAD_DROP_RETRY_SPAM_LIMIT (default 8
# lines; 0 disables the watchdog); the pattern is anchored on the
# `Attempt:` prefix so test-failure text that QUOTES the phrase
# (pty_harness's shutdownPty StateError) never trips the kill.
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/load_drop_retry.sh <main-log> <retry-log> -- <cmd...> "<targets>"
#   (interface unchanged from the PR #2347 one-shot — callers need nothing)
#
#   <main-log>   the path of the caller's own --file-reporter=json:<main-log>
#                (passed as part of <cmd...>) that junit/duration consumers
#                read — attempt-1 evidence is never clobbered; also names
#                the <main-log>.console capture;
#   <retry-log>  base path for the reruns' reporter logs: rerun k writes
#                <retry-log>.rerunK (kept separate so the main log is never
#                overwritten; rerun evidence only — no consumer reads it);
#   <cmd...>     the full dart test invocation INCLUDING its own
#                --file-reporter flag; the FINAL argument is the quoted,
#                space-separated target list (word-split here).
#
# Exit: 0 when the run (or a rerun) is green; the failing exit code
# otherwise. Coverage consumers are safe: every rerun inherits
# --coverage=coverage, so healed files' hits land in the same coverage/
# dir the gate merges.
set -euo pipefail
# TARGETS/RERUN_TARGETS expand unquoted below (word-split by design — the
# caller passes a quoted, space-separated list). Glob-off: a path carrying
# glob metacharacters must never expand (PR #2347 review digest).
set -f

usage() {
  echo "usage: $0 <main-log> <retry-log> -- <cmd...> \"<targets>\"" >&2
  exit 2
}

[ "$#" -ge 5 ] || usage
MAIN_LOG=$1
RETRY_LOG=$2
[ "${3:-}" = "--" ] || usage
shift 3
CMD=("${@:1:$#-1}")       # command + flags (including --file-reporter=…)
TARGETS="${!#}"           # final arg: quoted, space-separated target list
[ -n "$TARGETS" ] || usage

CONSOLE="${MAIN_LOG}.console"
BACKOFF=${LOAD_DROP_RETRY_BACKOFF_S:-5}
MAX_RERUNS=${LOAD_DROP_RETRY_MAX_RERUNS:-2}
# Operator knobs are consumed by bash integer tests/arithmetic below. A
# sleep-style "5s" or other garbage must not disable the retry loop itself.
[[ "$BACKOFF" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || BACKOFF=5
[[ "$MAX_RERUNS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || MAX_RERUNS=2
SPAM_LIMIT="${LOAD_DROP_RETRY_SPAM_LIMIT:-8}"
[[ "$SPAM_LIMIT" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || SPAM_LIMIT=8

FIFO=""
WATCHDOG_PID=""
RUNNER_RC=""

cleanup() {
  if [ -n "$WATCHDOG_PID" ]; then
    kill "$WATCHDOG_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
  if [ -n "$FIFO" ]; then
    rm -f "$FIFO" 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
}
trap cleanup EXIT

# run_streamed [--append] — runs CMD+TARGETS with output streamed to the
# console capture (live CI log) under the gh-2381 exit-handshake watchdog;
# leaves the runner's exit code in RUNNER_RC. Single-writer named pipe: the
# runner's stdout+stderr feed a background tee, and `$!` IS the runner pid
# — an exact kill target with no pgrep topology guessing.
#
# The runner rides `setsid` (own process group) so the watchdog's wedge
# kill takes the WHOLE tree down: a killed dart test leaves its spawned
# children (pty CLIs, `dart run` chains, sleeps) holding the fifo's write
# end — without the group kill, `tee` never sees EOF and this wrapper
# hangs exactly like the wedge it is killing. After the runner exits, tee
# gets a short drain window (an orphan-held write end can keep it alive
# forever) and is then killed; the evidence is complete the moment the
# runner's writes land.
# run_streamed [--append] [segment-file] — the optional second argument is
# the failing-attempt segment file the rerun loop greps for its signature:
# one tee feeds the accumulated console AND the fresh per-attempt segment
# (their #2331 loop contract) plus the live CI log, from the same stream.
run_streamed() {
  local append=false
  [ "${1:-}" = "--append" ] && { append=true; shift; }
  local segment=""
  [ -n "${1:-}" ] && segment="$1"
  FIFO="${CONSOLE}.fifo"
  mkfifo "$FIFO"
  if $append; then
    if [ -n "$segment" ]; then
      tee -a "$CONSOLE" "$segment" < "$FIFO" &
    else
      tee -a "$CONSOLE" < "$FIFO" &
    fi
  else
    tee "$CONSOLE" < "$FIFO" &
  fi
  local tee_pid=$!
  if command -v setsid >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    setsid "${CMD[@]}" $TARGETS > "$FIFO" 2>&1 &
  else
    "${CMD[@]}" $TARGETS > "$FIFO" 2>&1 &
  fi
  local runner_pid=$!
  if [ "$SPAM_LIMIT" -gt 0 ]; then
    (
      # `read -t` is the poll timer: a BUILTIN — killing this subshell
      # mid-wait forks no `sleep` child for the job harness to report. The
      # spam count covers ONLY bytes appended during THIS run: the reruns
      # (--append) share the console with earlier attempts, whose wedge
      # spam must never insta-kill a healthy rerun before its first poll.
      exec 3< /dev/zero
      baseline=$(wc -c < "$CONSOLE" 2>/dev/null) || baseline=0
      while kill -0 "$runner_pid" 2>/dev/null; do
        n=$(tail -c +"$((baseline + 1))" "$CONSOLE" 2>/dev/null |
          grep -cE 'Attempt:[0-9]+ waiting for isolate') || n=0
        if [ "${n:-0}" -ge "$SPAM_LIMIT" ]; then
          echo "load_drop_retry: exit-handshake wedge — $n 'waiting for isolate' spam lines; SIGKILL the wedged runner's process group (results are already in the reporter, coverage is per-suite incremental; gh-2381)" >&2
          kill -9 -- "-$runner_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
          kill -9 "$runner_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
          break
        fi
        read -t 1 -u 3 || true
      done
    ) &
    WATCHDOG_PID=$!
  fi
  wait "$runner_pid" 2>/dev/null
  RUNNER_RC=$?
  if [ -n "$WATCHDOG_PID" ]; then
    kill "$WATCHDOG_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
    WATCHDOG_PID=""
  fi
  # Drain window: on the wedge path the group kill closed every write end
  # and tee EOFs on its own; on the normal path orphan-held writers can
  # keep tee alive indefinitely — cap the drain and kill it.
  exec 3< /dev/zero
  local i
  for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do
    kill -0 "$tee_pid" 2>/dev/null || break
    read -t 0.2 -u 3 || true
  done
  kill "$tee_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
  wait "$tee_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
  rm -f "$FIFO" 2>/dev/null || true
  FIFO=""
}

# Attempt 1 — the command exactly as the step defines it (its own
# --file-reporter=json:<main-log> is part of CMD; dart accumulates repeated
# reporter flags, so the wrapper must not add a second one).
set +e
run_streamed
RC=$RUNNER_RC
set -e

RERUNS=0
SEGMENT="$CONSOLE"     # the FAILING attempt's own output (detection input)
REPORTER="$MAIN_LOG"   # that attempt's reporter log (rerun inventory input)

while [ "$RC" -ne 0 ] && [ "$RERUNS" -lt "$MAX_RERUNS" ]; do
  # Detection gates WHETHER this wrapper reruns at all, on TWO transient
  # families read from the FAILING attempt's OWN segment — a healed
  # attempt-1 line living in the accumulated console can never re-arm the
  # loop:
  #   family 1 (#2331) — the loopback-ws drop signature;
  #   family 2 (gh-2381) — the engine-abandonment evidence: the attempt's
  #   reporter log records a started-but-never-finished test
  #   (--unfinished) or an invocation target with NO suite event at all
  #   (--loaded complement), i.e. Engine.run() died mid-queue. Trusted
  #   ONLY when the reporter log exists and is non-empty: a missing log
  #   (crash before the reporter flushed) degrades to the console evidence
  #   alone — never "every target is suspicious" (no-blind-rerun).
  # A real assertion failure, compile error, or timeout never pairs
  # `Failed to load "…"` with ws text nor leaves an abandoned inventory —
  # with neither transient the failure is deterministic runner territory:
  # exit here, loud, no rerun.
  HAS_REPORTER=false
  if [ -s "$REPORTER" ]; then HAS_REPORTER=true; fi
  DROPPED=""
  if grep -qE 'Connection closed before full header was received|Connection reset by peer' \
    "$SEGMENT"; then
    DROPPED=$(awk '/Failed to load/ && (/Connection closed before full header was received/ || /Connection reset by peer/)' \
      "$SEGMENT" |
      sed -E -e 's/.*Failed to load "([^"]+)".*/\1/' -e 't' -e 's/.*Failed to load ([^:"]+):.*/\1/' |
      sort -u)
  fi
  REPORTER_FAILED=""
  REPORTER_UNFINISHED=""
  REPORTER_LOADED=""
  if $HAS_REPORTER; then
    REPORTER_FAILED=$(python3 scripts/gate_failed_targets.py "$REPORTER")
    REPORTER_UNFINISHED=$(python3 scripts/gate_failed_targets.py --unfinished "$REPORTER")
    REPORTER_LOADED=$(python3 scripts/gate_failed_targets.py --loaded "$REPORTER")
  fi
  NEVER_LOADED=""
  if $HAS_REPORTER; then
    for t in $TARGETS; do
      if printf '%s\n' "$REPORTER_LOADED" | grep -Fxq -- "$t"; then continue; fi
      if printf '%s\n' "$DROPPED" | grep -Fxq -- "$t"; then continue; fi
      NEVER_LOADED="$NEVER_LOADED$t"$'\n'
    done
    NEVER_LOADED=$(printf '%s' "$NEVER_LOADED" | sed '/^$/d' | sort -u)
  fi
  TRANSIENT=$(printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n' "$DROPPED" "$REPORTER_UNFINISHED" \
    "$NEVER_LOADED" | sed '/^$/d' | sort -u)
  if [ -z "$TRANSIENT" ]; then
    echo "load_drop_retry: failure carries no loopback-ws drop signature (no abandoned inventory either) — not rerunning" >&2
    exit "$RC"
  fi
  # WHAT to rerun is the FULL failed inventory of the failing attempt, not
  # just the transient files (PR #2347 review round 1, blocking): union
  # the transient targets with every failed suite the attempt's reporter
  # recorded (gate_failed_targets.py — failure AND error results, load
  # failures via the hidden `loading <path>` tests; missing/unparsable log
  # = clean empty). A co-occurring real failure is therefore IN the rerun
  # and fails it — the shard stays red; an attempt whose ONLY losses are
  # transient heals.
  RERUN_TARGETS=$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$TRANSIENT" "$REPORTER_FAILED" | sed '/^$/d' | sort -u)
  if [ -z "$RERUN_TARGETS" ]; then
    echo "load_drop_retry: transient signature present but no failed-file inventory — not rerunning blind" >&2
    exit "$RC"
  fi

  RERUNS=$((RERUNS + 1))
  echo "🔁 load-drop retry (#2331): rerun $RERUNS/$MAX_RERUNS after ${BACKOFF}s drain backoff:" >&2
  printf '%s\n' "$RERUN_TARGETS" | sed 's/^/   /' >&2
  if [ "$BACKOFF" -gt 0 ]; then sleep "$BACKOFF"; fi
  BACKOFF=$((BACKOFF * 2))

  RETRY_CMD=()
  for arg in "${CMD[@]}"; do
    case "$arg" in
      --file-reporter=*) ;;            # rerun writes its own evidence log
      *) RETRY_CMD+=("$arg") ;;
    esac
  done

  SEGMENT="${CONSOLE}.rerun$RERUNS"
  REPORTER="${RETRY_LOG}.rerun$RERUNS"
  RETRY_CMD+=("--file-reporter=json:$REPORTER")
  set +e
  CMD=("${RETRY_CMD[@]}")
  TARGETS="$RERUN_TARGETS"  # the rerun drives the transient/failed inventory
  run_streamed --append "$SEGMENT"
  RC=$RUNNER_RC
  set -e
done

if [ "$RC" -eq 0 ]; then
  if [ "$RERUNS" -gt 0 ]; then
    echo "✅ load-drop retry: healed — dropped file(s) green on rerun $RERUNS" >&2
  fi
  exit 0
fi
echo "❌ load-drop retry: still red after $RERUNS rerun(s) (exit $RC) — failing loudly" >&2
exit "$RC"

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. This file is
the agent ENTRY document: the harness merges it into the system prompt with
a ~19 KB entry budget, so it must stay small enough to be fully visible.
Ceiling: **≤ 300 lines / ≤ 20 KB** — enforced by
`scripts/check_agents_md_size.sh` (pre-commit hook via `ci_fast_gate.sh` +
the CI `static` job). Subsystem essays live in `docs/` — index:
`docs/README.md`. Keep entries factual: paths, commands, invariants.

## Module map

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph CORE["SDK - flutter_agent_harness, pure Dart (lib/)"]
        AI["ai: providers, agent loop, sessions, compaction"]
        TOLS["tools: approval, redact, hashline, memory"]
        HOSTS["hosts: shared wiring, messaging, a2a, hub"]
    end
    subgraph PKG["packages/ - sibling Dart packages"]
        FAUI["fa_ui: widgets incl. trajectory"]
        DAP["dap_hub, fa_llm, fa_llm_mock"]
    end
    CLI["fa CLI - bin/ + lib/src/cli: TUI, slash commands, headless"]
    APP["Flutter app - flutter_app/: desktop, mobile, web shells"]
    EXT["Browser extension - browser_ext/ + lib/src/browser + serve_bridge"]
    OFFICE["Office add-in - office_addin/ + FA_HOST=office host"]
    GOLDEN["UI golden & styles - golden tests, themes, ui tests"]
    NETW["fa_network - external Go backend + network clients"]
    CORE --> CLI
    CORE --> APP
    CORE --> EXT
    PKG --> APP
    PKG --> CLI
    APP --> OFFICE
    CLI --> NETW
    APP --> NETW
    EXT --> NETW
    GOLDEN --> APP
    GOLDEN --> FAUI
```

## Project layout — one line per subsystem

Full subsystem reference: `docs/agents/sdk-subsystems.md` (SDK) +
`docs/agents/flutter-app-subsystems.md` (app/packages/repo-level).

**SDK core (`lib/`, pure Dart):**

- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers, session modes, per-tool overrides, critical-bash interceptor, per-turn grants.
- `lib/src/tools/` — `ask`/`request_secret`/media tools, `read` selectors + archives + sqlite, background shell jobs, availability + load modes.
- `lib/src/env/` — `ExecutionEnv` impls: `LocalShell` (setsid, killTree, drain caps, self-signal immunity), session-correlation vars, in-memory default.
- `lib/src/agent/` — FinalizeGate, tool pairing, session image registry.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — trajectory ledger core; goldens under `test/trajectory/goldens/`.
- `lib/src/redact/` — layered secret redaction (prompt, tool args, output, logs).
- `lib/src/hashline/` — `[path#TAG]` patch language (SWAP/DEL/INS, stale-tag rejection).
- `lib/src/compaction/` — branch summarization + AutoCompactor → policy: `docs/compaction.md`.
- `lib/src/lsp/`, `lib/src/mcp/` — `lsp` + MCP protocol tooling (lazy servers, pure-Dart transports).
- `lib/src/model_roles/` — roles/fallbacks/keyring/watchdogs + provider catalog; `lib/src/ttsr/` — streaming-interrupt rules.
- `lib/src/skills/`, `lib/src/prompts/` — skills discovery; AGENTS/CLAUDE/GOAL/DESIGN auto-merge into the system prompt.
- `lib/src/task/`, `lib/src/messaging/`, `lib/src/session/attach/` — subagents, inbox fabric, attached sessions → `docs/subagents/README.md`.
- `lib/src/memory/` — long-term memory (hosted `flutter_agent_memory` package) → pitfalls: `docs/memory-churn.md`.
- `lib/src/a2a/` — Agent2Agent client/server/manager (`fa serve --a2a`).
- `bin/fah.dart` + `lib/src/cli/` — the `fa` CLI: REPL, slash commands, headless/serve modes → `docs/agents/cli.md`.
- `lib/src/cube/` — fa_cube sandbox profiles → `docs/cubes.md`; `lib/src/cli/hep.dart` — HEP event protocol → `docs/hep.md`.
- `lib/src/web_search/` — `web_search` (DDG keyless → keyed providers); `tool/fa-clip/` — native macOS pasteboard helper.

**packages/ + app shells:**

- `packages/fa_ui/` — reusable widgets (incl. trajectory) → `docs/agents/fa-ui.md`; `dap_hub`, `fa_llm`, `fa_llm_mock` → `docs/dap.md`.
- `flutter_app/` — the Flutter app (desktop/mobile/web) → `docs/agents/flutter-app.md`; services one-liner: `docs/agents/services.md`; JS apps: `docs/agents/js-apps.md`; HomeKit/Calendar/CodeMie: `docs/agents/system-integrations.md`.
- `browser_ext/` + `lib/src/browser/` + `bin/serve_bridge.dart` — browser extension + WebSocket bridge → `docs/browser-extension.md`.
- `office_addin/` + FA_HOST=office app host — Office add-in → `docs/outlook-addin.md`.
- `fa_network` — external Go backend bridged via the DAP hub (channel-id caveats: `docs/dap.md` §14).
- `site/`, `scripts/`, `docs/subagents/` — landing page (privacy sync), gates + codegen, subagents master plan → `docs/agents/flutter-app-subsystems.md`.

## Hard architecture rules (stay inline)

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.
- Barrel `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart`: grouped **APPEND-ONLY** export
  sections — one `// ── <subsystem> ──` header per group, sorted by path
  within a group, new exports append to their group. No mini-barrels, no
  re-sorting (gh-1232).
- God-file ceiling: no `.dart` file over **2800** lines (crap4dart `loc`
  gate). Target < 2000 for primary files; split by concern into `part`
  files — never by extracting public API.

## Working in parallel (shared checkout + worktrees)

Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked; run no
heavy commands (full suites/analyze) in it; never `git stash` the user's
WIP; talk to peer agents through the messaging fabric, not their files.
Worktrees only if genuinely required — ask first, create detached under
`.worktrees/<name>/` from the remote tracking ref, remove when done.
Full policy: `docs/agents/parallel-worktrees.md`.

## Memory (footnote)

Before any non-trivial task, **search memory first** (`memory_search`,
then `memory_list` for fuzzy topics). Scopes: **project** = this repo
(`.fah/memory/note/` since gh-2185 — local-only, not committed; the
user's files: read freely, write only via `memory_add`), **user** = global/private. `memory_add` stores durable facts
only; supersede by delete + add — never leave solved problems to rot. The
host recomposes the `<memory>` prompt section after every add; tool wiring
is `memoryTools` + `lib/src/memory/`. Churn pitfalls: `docs/memory-churn.md`;
usage details: `docs/agents/memory-usage.md`.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done: coverage first (`test/goldens/` + `golden_guard_test.dart`
map), real fonts (`ensureGoldenFonts`), full frames (1280x800 / 390x844),
determinism, eyes on pixels after `--update-goldens`, green
`flutter test test/goldens` + `scripts/check_goldens.py` (orphan snapshots
hard-fail). Full rules: `docs/agents/golden-tests.md`.

## Prompts live outside Dart code

Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (YAML frontmatter,
`{{token}}` placeholders) — never string literals in `.dart`. After
editing: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` regenerates the `.g.dart`
files (`test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart` gates drift); Codex catalog
refresh: `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Details:
`docs/agents/prompts.md`.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The hook is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI classifies
PRs through the same script (`--dry-run`) — one classifier, one threshold
set, hook/CI parity via `GATE_STAGE` markers. Path rules: docs/markdown/
prompts-only → size + analyze; lib/bin/test/pubspec → +tests, coverage,
CRAP, dup, dupx; `test/integration/**` → +integration-mock;
flutter_app/packages → +flutter; scripts/.github → everything. Invariants:

- analyze + format clean; `dart test` green — **deterministic-only**
  (mock LLM; live models never in the gate; `llm`-tagged files run only in
  the tag-only provider smoke + nightly).
- Line coverage of `lib/` ≥ 80%; jscpd < 1% core / < 3.7% app; cross-module
  dup < 0.31%; CRAP ratchet: core 12.0, app 30.0 (thresholds only-down);
  ≤ 2800 lines per `.dart` file; AGENTS.md ceiling (top of this file).
- Red-in-≥2-distinct-SHA-runs flakes quarantine via
  `scripts/test_quarantine.json`; nightly keeps running quarantined files.

Full gate text: `docs/agents/quality-gates.md`; CI workflows: `docs/ci.md`.

## Cross-platform parity

Every shared setting and interactive prompt type exists on BOTH the CLI
and the Flutter app unless fundamentally impossible — then it MUST be in
`cliOnlySettings`/`appOnlySettings` (`lib/src/parity/settings_registry.dart`)
with the reason; run `dart test test/parity/`. Host capabilities (issue
#1079): every host-wiring capability declares its 7-host matrix state AT
BIRTH (`on` / `off(reason)` / `transport`) via `wireAgentCore` — `off` is
invisible everywhere; extensions are declared surface, SDK invariants have
no override point. Full rules: `docs/agents/cross-platform-parity.md`.

## Commits and releases

- Commit as `ai.teammate <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (set repo-locally);
  subjects `type(scope): ...`. Release-path automation MUST use the
  fa-release-bot GitHub App token — never a PAT or `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
- Every push to main cuts an annotated tag (`scripts/auto_release.sh`);
  the tag is the single version source (pubspecs stay `0.0.0-dev`);
  releases go DRAFT-first and publish at `release-provenance` only with
  signed SHA256SUMS attached. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only (`## Unreleased`).
- `packages/fa_llm` publishes per `fa_llm-v*` tag (first publish of a new
  package is manual); every lockfile is committed and enforced
  (`scripts/check_lockfiles.sh`); TestFlight external-group + store
  pipelines have required repo variables.

Full text: `docs/agents/commits-releases.md`.

## Bench

Bench knobs (agent timeouts, stall/watch, `FA_CONN_DEBUG`, hang replay,
report semantics) → `docs/bench.md` (round-3 knobs: issue #1392).

## Docs index

`docs/README.md` indexes every canonical doc (agents/, memory-churn,
compaction, dap, cubes, redaction, hep, ci, bench, browser-extension,
outlook-addin, …). New docs must be listed there.

## PR Description

Closes #2381
### Root Cause
- v1.0.766's PTY shard 2/3 died from a three-layer chain: the vm-service loopback WS died mid-coverage-gather (the #2331 load class); the test_core engine's run loop threw with its queue still pending (3 tests in flight, 10 suites never loaded — proven by the shard's own reporter: allSuites 26, 16 suite events, testStart 101 vs testDone 98); the abandoned suites' live pty2 children blocked the VM exit handshake (`Attempt:N waiting for isolate _waitForExitCode`, ×2348) until the 40-minute kill concluded the job `cancelled` → Quality gate red → no signed SHA256SUMS → `pin_release.sh` refused (`E_PIN_PROVENANCE_MISSING`) → "Advance vpinned marker" red.
- The watchdog retrigger healed the wedge but red'd `Hostile ambient env`: `agent_cli_waiting_integration_test.dart` AC1 (#2260) reads `running.json` right after `pumpEventQueue()`, but the settle-side manifest removal is an unawaited file-IO chain — under load the assertion observed the pre-removal manifest (same SHA green in the original run).

### Fix
- `scripts/load_drop_retry.sh`: the sharded legs' wrapper now SIGKILLs a wedged runner on sustained `Attempt:N waiting for isolate` console spam (counted over the attempt's own fresh console bytes; results are already in the file-reporter; coverage is per-suite incremental) instead of burning the shard budget, and heals the abandonment: unfinished-test suites + never-loaded invocation targets join the bounded rerun inventory (merged on top of #2379's bounded loop + drain backoff, which landed on main mid-leg) — real failures join the rerun and keep the shard red; a missing reporter never widens the inventory.
- `scripts/gate_failed_targets.py`: `--unfinished` (started tests with no `testDone` → their suite paths) and `--loaded` (suite-event paths) projections; the default failed-paths contract for `FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES` is unchanged (verified: run 45200064457's real shard artifact → `--unfinished` = the 3 in-flight suites, `--loaded` = 16).
- `test/cli/agent_cli_waiting_integration_test.dart` AC1: the manifest leave is now observed via a bounded load-tolerant wait (gh-2378 house shape) with a loud fail at the bound.

### Test Coverage
- `test/scripts/gate_failed_targets_test.dart`: 15 tests — unfinished/loaded projections incl. a fixture of the REAL abandonment log.
- `test/scripts/load_drop_retry_test.dart`: 18 tests — the #2379 bounded-loop contract (AC1-13, merged) + gh-2381 AC20-24 driving the real wrapper with stubbed runners: wedge spam → group-kill → exact abandoned-inventory rerun → heals; rerun-still-red stays loud; exit-70 unfinished and never-loaded both rerun; the --append baseline keeps a rerun from being insta-killed by attempt-1 spam (caught by the real-artifact verification).
- `test/cli/agent_cli_waiting_integration_test.dart`: 29 tests pass.
- Full `dart test --exclude-tags integration,browser-ext,llm` suite: 15006 passed, 16 skipped, 0 failed (exit 0).

### Notes
- No product-code changes — CI infra + one flaky test; the wrapper's fast path (green run, no transient signature) exits 0 with a single invocation, byte-identical behavior to before.
- The gh-2290 watchdog retrigger stays as the outer net; this fix turns the wedge class from a cancelled 40-minute burn into a minutes-scoped targeted rerun.
- The "Advance vpinned marker" refusal is by-design provenance gating; it recovers once the ref goes green.

      # gh-1300: the AOT binary built once per run by fa-aot-build. The
      # guard FAILS the shard loudly if the artifact is missing or dead —
      # a silent JIT fallback would hide the optimization from AC1's
      # before/after numbers.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/sqlite3-native-assets-prewarm
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: fa-aot-bin
          path: fa-local/bundle
      # Artifact zips do NOT preserve the exec bit (download-artifact
      # README: "post-download the file is no longer guaranteed to be set
      # as an executable"). Run 37446280743: `test -x` below failed
      # silently ~20 ms in on EVERY shard — the gate went red before a
      # single test ran. Restore the mode the build job shipped; the
      # smoke below still verifies the restored binary is executable and
      # boots (never a silent JIT fallback). Content integrity is not
      # affected: download-artifact digest-validates (digest-mismatch:
      # error default), so this chmod only ever touches the verified
      # bundle the fa-aot-build job produced.
      - name: Restore exec bit (artifact zips drop permissions)
        run: chmod +x fa-local/bundle/bin/fa
      - name: Smoke the AOT binary (fail loud, never JIT-fallback)
        run: |
          test -x fa-local/bundle/bin/fa
          ./fa-local/bundle/bin/fa --version
      - name: dart test --tags integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
        env:
          # gh-1300 FA_BIN seam: every CLI spawn (pty_harness + the
          # headless helpers via faCliCommand) runs the AOT binary —
          # ~1 s per spawn instead of the JIT VM+CFE compile (~30 s on
          # loaded ARM runners). Per-test isolation is unchanged.

          # backstop. AC6: the quarantine filter drops flake-quarantined

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Shard-manifest assert (issue #283, AC1/E4): proves a shard manifest
covers EXACTLY the intended suite before any test runs.

Checks (all must hold, each failure is loud):
    1. union of all shard selections == the full suite on disk
       (root/**/*_test.dart minus --exclude matches minus integration);
    2. pairwise intersection of shard selections is empty — a test file is
       executed by exactly ONE shard;
    3. zero excluded files (e.g. host-locked goldens) leak into any shard.

Run from the package whose test/ dir is being sharded:

    cd packages/fa_ui
    python3 ../../scripts/assert_shard_manifest.py \
        ../../scripts/faui_test_shards.json --shards 3 --exclude golden

Tag-scoped manifests (issue #931: the integration shards) pass --tags so
both the selection AND the expected suite derive from the same matcher:

    python3 scripts/assert_shard_manifest.py \
        scripts/test_integration_shards.json --shards 3 \
        --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm

The --exclude-tag form (gh-1199 AC1) asserts the live boundary too: the
expected suite is tagged-minus-excluded, and any excluded-tag file
reaching a selection is a loud leak.

Delegates the actual selection to shard_files.py (same interpreter the CI
test step uses), so the assert can never drift from what CI really runs.

Pure stdlib. Exit 0 on success, 1 on any violation.
"""

# (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p build/test-results
          # Issue #2331: under CI-leg load the dart test loader's loopback ws
          # to a spawning test VM dies mid-handshake ("Failed to load …:
          # Connection closed before full header was received / Connection
          # reset by peer") — an arbitrary victim file, 6/6 occurrences on
          # this leg family. The wrapper re-runs ONLY the failed inventory
          # (gh-1026 rerun-only-failed discipline), bounded ≤2 reruns with a
          # drain backoff; real failures carry no ws-drop signature and stay
          # loud. junit below still reads the attempt-1 main log — a healed
          # rerun writes to …retry.json.rerunK.
          bash scripts/load_drop_retry.sh \
            "build/test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            "build/test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.retry.json" \
            -- \
            dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:build/test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            "$targets"
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            build/test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            build/test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        run: |
          mkdir -p build/test-results
          # Issue #2227: the trio rides NO quarantine filter (gh-1033: the
          # CLI coverage ratchet needs these hits on every core/shared PR),
          # so the #2331 loopback-ws load-drop family reached this leg
          # unhealed — a dropped loader ws reds the gate on an arbitrary
          # victim file while every test that ran was green (4/4 jsr_cli
          # reds were loader drops, never assertions). Same one-shot
          # wrapper as the sharded legs: a dropped file reruns ONCE (the
          # rerun inherits --coverage=coverage, so healed hits land in
          # this shard's coverage dir); real failures carry no ws-drop
          # signature and stay loud. No junit consumer reads these logs —
          # the trio feeds the lcov merge only.

**Verified sound (with evidence):**

The NEVER_LOADED projection only arms on genuine engine abandonment — I verified empirically with the real reporter (test 1.33.0): compile errors, nonexistent files, and normal suites ALL emit suite events with repo-relative paths matching target strings; only true mid-queue death leaves targets unloaded. So deterministic failures do NOT trigger reruns. The doc-comment claim holds.
3. `--unfinished` semantics — pending map popped on every testDone; torn-tail lines degrade to unfinished → rerun → correct transient classification.
4. Watchdog design — per-atempt baseline (AC24 pins), `Attempt:`-prefix anchoring (avoids quoted-phrase false trips), group-kill safe (PGID=runner_pid only exists under setsid), spam-kill self-heals even on false trips (unfinished inventory reruns). Coverage claim verified against test_core source (writeCoverage per-suite, engine.dart:285-287).
5. Rerun inventory union (TRANSIENT ∪ REPORTER_FAILED) keeps co-ocurring real failures red — pinned by AC7/AC8/AC21.

9. Ticket AC satisfaction: the PR closes gh-2381 — root cause addressed at all three layers (wedge kill, abandonment rerun, flaky AC1 wait). The vpinned marker refusal is by-design provenance gating (recovers when ref goes green) — no change needed there, and the PR explains it.

**Findings worth raising:**

Honestly, after this deep a pass, I found no BLOCKING or IMPORTANT issues. Candidates:

(a) **Watchdog re-scan cost** (tail -c +baseline | grep per second over growing console) — O(atempt console bytes) per poll. For the PTY leg the console can be tens of MB over a healthy run; re-grepping the whole fresh range every second for the run's duration is wasteful but bounded (~MB/s grep — negligible on CI runners). The wedge is killed in seconds anyway; a healthy run pays the grep only while the runner lives. NIT/digest. Actually — hmm, per-poll cost is O(console-so-far) and polls are 1/s over the whole run duration. For a 10-min shard producing 10MB, cumulative grep ≈ 3GB total ≈ a few CPU-seconds. Negligible. → digest line, not a thread.

(b) **`REPORTER_UNFINISHED`/`NEVER_LOADED` are computed even when DROPPED already armed a rerun** — three python3 invocations per failed attempt — negligible cost. Not even digest-worthy.

(d) **`mkfifo` failure on a stale fifo after a SIGKILL'd prior wrapper** — edge-of-edge; the wrapper only SIGKILLs its runner children, not itself; if the wrapper itself is SIGKILLed (timeout kill by CI), the trap doesn't run and the fifo file leaks → the NEXT attempt... wait, actually! This is interesting: on CI, the STEP (run: bash load_drop_retry.sh ...) is killed by the job timeout (40 min) — SIGKILL/SIGTERM to the step process group. If the wrapper is killed while a fifo exists mid-run_streamed, the fifo leaks at build/test-results/...console.fifo. But the next attempt would be a FRESH job/run (the timeout concluded the job) — a new workspace? GitHub runners get fresh workspaces per job... For a retriggered run it's a fresh runner VM. Local: ci_fast_gate pre-commit reruns in the same workspace — a stale fifo at the same path would make `mkfifo` fail → set -e exit 2 → the gate reds confusingly instead of running tests. Hmm — but for the pre-commit gate the wrapper is invoked per stage; would a prior SIGKILL'd wrapper leave the fifo? Only if IT was killed mid-run by an external kill. Extremely rare, self-inflicted only by the user killing the gate mid-run. And even then, `mkfifo` failure → loud red, trivialy fixed by deleting the file. The fa harness tracks spawned processes; a stray sleep child under a killed watchdog subshell might show up in job listings. That's why they avoided sleep.) — the cleanest no-process timer: open fd 3 on an empty regular file? read returns EOF instantly → spin on EOF... `read -t 1 -u 3` on EOF returns immediately → tight loop around the whole watchdog body → worse. On a fifo with no writer: `mkfifo` + `exec 3<> "$fifo"` — opening a fifo O_RDWR never blocks! `exec 3<>"$fifo"` succeeds immediately; read then BLOCKS (no data, no writer) until the 1s timeout → TRUE sleep, zero CPU, zero child processes. Hmm — wait, careful: `read -t` on a fifo fd — when the runner (the only writer) closes/exits, the read returns EOF instantly → the watchdog then loops hot on EOF?? The watchdog loop is `while kill -0 runner_pid; do ... read -t 1 -u 3 || true; done` — with an O_RDWR fifo fd, after all OTHER writers exit, read on O_RDWR fifo BLOCKS (no data) — O_RDWR readers never see EOF unless... for a fifo opened O_RDWR, read blocks forever when empty (the process itself holds the write end). Actually POSIX: EOF is returned when all WRITE ends are closed AND you opened read-only. With O_RDWR, your own write end counts as open → read never EOFs → blocks. ✓ perfect timer.

"⚠️ IMPORTANT — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge."

The dart test shard with --concurrency=4 on a hosted 4-core runner: 1 core peged by a bash busy-loop → tests get ~3 cores instead of 4 → the leg slows modestly but its load-sensitivity rises. The original 40-min wedges were attributed to "SM dispatch waves pack the hosted pool" etc. The marginal harm is real but speculative in magnitude.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the watchdog poll timer busy-spins ~1 core for the entire lifetime of every attempt**

The new watchdog uses `read -t 1 -u 3` with fd 3 opened from `/dev/zero` as its 1-second poll timer (`scripts/load_drop_retry.sh:170` + `:181`, reused at `:195`/`:199` for the drain loop). `read` on `/dev/zero` never blocks and never yields a newline, so the builtin loops on instant `read()` syscalls for the full second — this is a hot poll loop, not a timer.

Measured on this checkout (the real script, stubbed runner):

- 30 s wall run with a sleeping stub: **30.25 CPU-seconds consumed** (8.20 user + 22.05 sys) ≈ one full core pinned for the whole run.
- Sampled at 3 s elapsed: the wrapper bash at **99.3% CPU** (`ps -o pcpu`), while the stub itself slept at ~0%.

Why it matters: this watchdog now runs on every attempt of every wrapped leg — the PTY integration shards (ci.yml:1470), the core unit shards (ci.yml:1011), the jsr trio (ci.yml:1047), and the local fast gate (ci_fast_gate.sh:252). A healthy shard run pays one pinned core for its full duration (a 5-min shard ≈ 5 core-minutes stolen), and the PTY legs are precisely the load-sensitive class (FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE, "SM dispatch waves pack the hosted pool") whose flakes this PR heals — the fix adds sustained CPU contention to the conditions that induce the failure.

The intent behind `/dev/zero` ("killing this subshell mid-wait forks no `sleep` child for the job harness to report") can be kept with a true zero-CPU, zero-child timer: open a watchdog-private FIFO `O_RDWR` — `exec 3<>"${CONSOLE}.wdg.fifo"` — an O_RDWR fifo never EOFs (the process's own write end holds it), so `read -t 1 -u 3` blocks silently until the timeout. Verified in this sandbox: 3 × `read -t 1` polls = 3009 ms elapsed, **0.00 CPU** (`/usr/bin/time`: 0% of wall). Add the fifo to the existing `cleanup` trap. (Do NOT point fd 3 at the console fifo itself — reading it would steal the runner's output from `tee`.)

Alternatively `sleep 1` would also work but forks the child you deliberately avoided, so the fifo timer is the closer match to the stated constraint. The ≤1 s drain loop at `:195` is bounded and can keep the `/dev/zero` form or take the same fix.
